description: Executable Java 25 and Spring Boot 4 modernization tasks for the Order Service.

tasks.description: Upgrade the Order Service backend to the Java 25 and Spring Boot 4.x target while preserving its order API behavior.
tasks.reason: Addresses assessment issues: Java 8 end-of-life baseline, Spring Boot 2.7.18 end of OSS support, javax-to-jakarta blocker, and deprecated WebMvcConfigurerAdapter.
tasks.requirements: Scope: app/Java - Spring Boot/Order Service backend only. Upgrade Java, Spring Boot, and the managed framework stack to the Spring Boot 4.x / Java 25-compatible target. Migrate all identified javax.persistence, javax.validation, and javax.validation.Valid imports to Jakarta APIs. Replace the deprecated WebMvcConfigurerAdapter configuration while retaining the existing /api/** CORS route coverage and permitted methods. Preserve the existing REST endpoints, validation semantics, H2-backed persistence behavior, and test behavior. Risk: Spring Boot 4 / Hibernate changes can alter JPA and validation behavior; the current permissive CORS origin must not be broadened. Validation: run the complete Maven test suite and package build using an actual JDK 25 installation, and confirm the existing API tests remain green.
tasks.summary: Upgraded the Order Service backend from Java 8 / Spring Boot 2.7.18 to Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.1.1, passing through a Spring Boot 3.5.16 / Java 21 intermediate hop. Migrated all javax.persistence and javax.validation (including javax.validation.Valid) imports to jakarta.* in Order.java and OrderController.java. Replaced the deprecated WebMvcConfigurerAdapter with WebMvcConfigurer in WebConfig.java, keeping the /api/** CORS mapping, permissive origin ("*"), and permitted methods (GET, POST, PATCH) byte-for-byte unchanged. Updated pom.xml (spring-boot-starter-parent, java.version/compiler source-target, spring-boot-starter-web -> spring-boot-starter-webmvc) and added spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test / spring-boot-starter-data-jpa-test to satisfy Spring Boot 4's test-module modularization; migrated OrderControllerTest.java from @MockBean to @MockitoBean (MockBean/SpyBean removed in Spring Boot 4.0) and fixed @WebMvcTest/@DataJpaTest import package relocations. Validated with mvn clean test-compile, mvn clean test, and mvn clean package using an actual installed JDK 25.0.2 distribution (not JDK 26) and Maven 3.9.16: BUILD SUCCESS, 20/20 backend tests passing (100%, matches the pre-migration baseline of 20/20), runnable JAR produced. The frozen pre-migration baseline folder src/test/test-cases/ was not modified. A CVE scan restricted to the dependencies actually managed by this upgrade (spring-boot-starter-webmvc, spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, spring-boot-starter-validation, hibernate-core, h2) found no new vulnerabilities; the pre-existing intentionally-pinned vulnerable log4j-core:2.14.1 and commons-text:1.9 were left untouched as they are explicitly in scope for the separate dependent task 003-remediate-dependency-cves. README.md tech-stack/prerequisites updated to reflect Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.1.1. Final committed state: Java 25 with Spring Boot 4.1.1 on branch modernize/java-20260909170843.

tasks.description: Capture the frozen Order Service behavior and external-dependency test strategy before modernization verification.
tasks.reason: Provides a stable regression specification for the requested post-migration integration verification.
tasks.requirements: Scope: app/Java - Spring Boot/Order Service source snapshot and existing backend/frontend test behavior. Capture the order API scenarios, H2 persistence assumptions, validation outcomes, and frontend build/test expectations. Freeze an infra-decision table selecting mocked external dependencies because this plan has no provisioned Azure environment. Risk: an incomplete baseline can conceal a behavior regression. Validation: baseline artifacts document all currently exercised backend tests and frontend test/build commands and identify the mock strategy for every external dependency.
tasks.summary: Snapshotted 'app/Java - Spring Boot/Order Service' to an isolated temp folder and built the frozen baseline exclusively from that snapshot. Ran the full backend suite (mvn test: BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 20, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 across OrderRepositoryTest, OrderServiceTest, OrderServiceUnitTest, OrderControllerTest) and the frontend suite/build (npm test: 4/4 passed via node --test; npm run build: succeeded, 36 modules transformed) from the snapshot. Authored src/test/test-cases/test-cases.md documenting the Order API contract, validation rules, H2 persistence assumptions (IDENTITY ids, @PrePersist createdAt, STRING-mapped status enum, DataSeeder seed rows), CORS/web config, the full backend test inventory, the frontend view-logic contract, and a frozen infra-decision table selecting MOCKED external dependencies for every dependency (H2 kept as embedded/in-process; no Azure resource, credential, or connection referenced or attempted anywhere in the baseline, per the no-provisioned-Azure-environment constraint). Added testdata/seeded-orders.json, testdata/sample-requests.json, and testdata/frontend-orders-fixture.json as frozen fixtures referenced by the spec. Copied only these frozen artifacts back into the live workspace under src/test/test-cases/ (production source untouched) and committed them on the current branch. This folder is now FROZEN.

tasks.description: Remediate confirmed and version-correlated dependency vulnerabilities without changing Order Service behavior.
tasks.reason: Addresses assessment issues: Log4Shell-related Log4j Core 2.14.1, Text4Shell-related Commons Text 1.9, and six npm audit advisories in frontend build tooling.
tasks.requirements: Scope: Order Service Maven dependencies and frontend package manifest/lockfile only. Upgrade Log4j Core and Commons Text to minimum patched stable versions, and remediate npm audit findings including Vite/esbuild and transitive browser tooling. Document breaking-change risk when a required fix is semver-major, particularly the Vite major upgrade. Do not include the separately deferred React 18 to 19 upgrade unless it is strictly required by the security fix. Treat H2 2.1.214 as version-aged rather than CVE-confirmed. Risk: dependency upgrades can change build tooling or runtime behavior; Java scanner confirmation requires credentials or an NVD API key. Validation: complete the Maven build and test suite, frontend npm test and build, rerun npm audit, and retain the final Java scanner result or explicitly document scanner-authentication limitations.
tasks.summary: Upgraded org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core 2.14.1 -> 2.25.4 and org.apache.commons:commons-text 1.9 -> 1.10.0 in the Order Service pom.xml, resolving all 7 log4j-core CVEs (including the Log4Shell family CVE-2021-44228/45046/45105/44832 plus 2025/2026 TLS/XML advisories) and the Text4Shell CVE-2022-42889. H2 2.1.214 was left unchanged (CVE-2022-45868 patch exists at 2.2.220 but is explicitly out of scope per task requirements: treated as version-aged only, no upgrade forced since no compatibility issue required it). Frontend: upgraded vite ^5.4.11 -> ^8.2.2 (semver-major) and its peer @vitejs/plugin-react ^4.3.4 -> ^6.1.1 in frontend/package.json, resolving all 6 npm audit advisory groups (baseline-browser-mapping, browserslist, esbuild, nanoid, postcss, vite) with zero React version change (react/react-dom confirmed still at 18.3.1; React 18->19 upgrade was not needed and not performed). npm audit before: 6 vulnerable packages / moderate=2,high=4,total=6; after: 0 vulnerable packages / total=0. Documented the vite major-upgrade breaking-change risk in summary.md (no vite.config.js changes required, plugin API surface unaffected). Validation: mvn clean test -> BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 20, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 (20/20 matching required baseline); frontend npm test -> 4/4 passed; frontend npm run build -> succeeded (20 modules transformed). Re-ran appmod-validate-cves-for-java after fixes: log4j-core and commons-text report zero remaining CVEs; only the explicitly out-of-scope H2 finding remains (no scanner-authentication limitation encountered). Changes committed directly on branch modernize/java-20260909170843 (commit cde8c8a7637cff1a98a0e62a73a741bc859f4784); no source code (.java/.jsx/.js) files were modified, dependency-only remediation with no behavior changes. Full details in .github/modernize/java-upgrade/20260909173554/summary.md.

tasks.description: Build integration tests for migrated Azure services and run post-migration verification
tasks.reason: Confirms the upgraded service preserves observable behavior using the baseline's mocked-dependency strategy; no Azure service is provisioned in this code-only plan.
tasks.requirements: Scope: migrated Order Service backend, H2 test configuration, and frontend verification workflow. Implement and run post-migration integration verification from the frozen baseline using mocked dependencies; do not require Azure credentials or resource identifiers. Cover the existing order API paths, validation behavior, persistence interactions, and the frontend test/build workflow affected by dependency remediation. Risk: mock-only verification cannot establish production Azure connectivity, which is out of scope. Validation: all frozen backend and frontend scenarios pass on the Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.x target, with any intentional behavior difference documented and accepted.
